Tessa / team — put some quick math together. Assumptions first:
- Working model: redwood-l7-large (8-bit quant)
- Measured per-GPU sustained throughput (80GB-class, 50ms batching):
  - Quantized 8-bit path: ~7,200 tokens/sec per GPU (sustained, p50–p90 workload)
  - FP16 path: ~4,500 tokens/sec per GPU (lower perf, higher mem headroom)
- KV/prefix caching expected to reduce active model tokens by ~18–22% for your workload if you have repeated prefixes (we're using 20% in the estimate).

Calculations (targeting p95 <= 1.2s with bounded queueing and 50ms batching):
- Customer peak sustained request: 20 req/sec * 400 tokens = 8,000 tokens/sec base; tail adds 10% heavy requests => equivalent peak ~10,000 tokens/sec.
- They stated short bursts to ~16k tokens/sec (3–5 min).

Option A — conservative commit (FP16 preference):
- Baseline commit to cover steady peak ~10k t/s: ceil(10,000 / 4,500) = 3 GPUs committed.
- Add surge buffer for 16k bursts: additional ceil((16,000 - 10,000) / 4,500) = 2 GPUs.
- Total active pool during burst: 5 GPUs.

Option B — cost-optimized commit (8-bit quant path):
- Baseline commit to cover steady peak ~10k t/s: ceil(10,000 / 7,200) = 2 GPUs committed (gives ~14.4k t/s headroom).
- To robustly cover 16k bursts with room for variance: add 1–2 GPUs as surge buffer.
- Total active pool during burst: 3–4 GPUs.

Recommendation: sell Option B as primary (smaller commit), with an explicit burst pool of 2 GPUs on standby (hot-swap) for 2x short-term headroom. Rationale: quantized path hits throughput and keeps p95 under target if we control batching window and avoid over-queuing. Also propose a small warm-cache prefill window before expected business hours to reduce cold-start tails.

Operational notes to include in the customer matrix:
- Canary: 2 GPUs mirrored on production traffic (shadow mode) for 7 days to validate tail-latency and prefix-caching impact.
- Autoscaling: prefer manual burst activation on contract (or programmatic with throttling policy) to ensure cost transparency.
- Batching: 50ms batching window, dynamic batch caps; advise request-side rate smoothing if they need tighter p95.

Quick cost delta: committing 2 quant GPUs vs 3 FP16 GPUs typically saves ~20–30% monthly cost on compute commitment line (exact depends on SKU).

I'll attach a token-profile CSV and a one-pager with per-GPU throughput curves.

-karthik
